title: Applied ML experiments runbook — Oct 6–12, 2025
content:
Weekly runbook + lab notes for the Applied ML research sprint (Oct 6–12, 2025). Purpose: capture hypotheses, short experiment results, unblock model onboarding, and hand off to infra/serving for QC and perf runs.

SUMMARY:
- Focus this week: evaluate post-training quantization (PTQ) impact on generation quality for two mid-sized open models, validate KV-cache behavior after quantization, and prototype a minimal onboarding checklist for opt-6.7b variants with quantization profile.
- Quick outcome: INT8 PTQ on the 13B candidate reduced GPU memory by ~36% and inference latency per token improved 10–18% on A100; however, small but measurable degradation on completions for domain QA (avg. ΔROUGE-L -1.8). KV-cache integrity tests passed for prefix lengths <= 1024 tokens but we saw jittered logits when using fused attention kernels on H100 with the quantized kernels.

MEETING NOTES (Oct 9 weekly sync):
Attendees: Anya, Marcus, Irene, Samir, Lena, DevOps: Patrick (10m).
- Decision: prioritize stability over max compression for next onboarding: target 6–8 bits mixed quant profiles for release candidate, not aggressive 4-bit PTQ, until we have human eval on targeted prompt sets.
- Action: Samir to run a 50-case human-judged evaluation on the most common product prompts by Fri (Jira AIINF-4123).
- Infra ask: Patrick needs the quantized wheel + docker image by Mon to run multi-GPU stress tests in staging.
- Follow-up: schedule a short handoff with Serving runtime owners to validate fallback policy (quantized -> float) on mismatch events.

EXPERIMENT LOGS (lab-style notes, rough):
1) PTQ sweep — model: raven-13b-open (candidate)
- Method: layerwise GPTQ-like PTQ tool, per-channel scales, 8-bit and 6-bit variants. No finetune.
- HW: A100-40GB and H100-80GB
- Metric slices: open-ended generation on product-QA set (n=300), pass@1 concordance for canonical answers, automatic metrics: ROUGE-L, BERTScore, perplexity on held-out validation chunk.
- Results (aggregate):
  - Float baseline: memory 23.4GB, avg token lat A100 18.6ms, ROUGE-L baseline 0.712.
  - 8-bit PTQ: memory 15.0GB (-35.9%), avg token lat A100 15.8ms (-15%), ROUGE-L 0.703 (Δ -0.009).
  - 6-bit PTQ: memory 11.8GB (-49.6%), avg token lat A100 14.8ms (-20%), ROUGE-L 0.687 (Δ -0.025).
- Notes: 6-bit shows visible hallucination on longer QA prompts (>200 tokens). Qual notes flagged by human raters: answer omission and excessive verbosity.

2) KV-cache integrity tests:
- Scenario: long prefix (>1024 tokens) with repeat-token patterns, force cache-miss/regeneration patterns.
- Observed: 8-bit PTQ maintained exact logits up to the first 1024 tokens. Beyond that, on H100 with fused attention+quantized-kernel, we observed small per-token logit drift causing top-3 token instability for ~2–3 tokens after a new chunk is injected.
- Hypothesis: mixed-precision accumulation differences in fused kernels + quantized weight rounding.
- Temporary mitigation: fall back to non-fused attention kernels for sequences >1024 until we validate kernel fixes. Filing infra ticket.

3) Onboarding prototype for opt-6.7b-quantized variant:
- Checklist (prototype):
  - artifacts: quantized weights tar.gz (sha256), tokenizer version, model card updates, eval prompt set (copy), config (seq_len, block_size), quant profile used.
  - smoke tests: seq generation sanity, attention visualizer snapshot, KV-cache regen test, perf baseline (1/2/4 batch sizes).
  - rollout steps: canary on Dedicated pool -> monitor latency & token-error rate -> expand if no regressions in 48h.
- Current status: artifacts produced (PR: serving-runtime#2786), smoke tests passing locally for 8-bit, failing KV-cache edge on H100.

HUMAN EVAL PLAN (quick):
- 50 prompts from product-QA + 30 prompts from long-form summarization. Each judged by 3 raters for correctness, factuality, and readability. Export schema in attached CSV (linked artifact in Jira). Goal: reach p<0.05 on degradation for correctness vs float baseline.
- Samir owns annotation batch; Lena to triage disagreements and prepare adjudicated gold set.

RISKS & OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Risk: aggressive quantization (<=6-bit) may reduce unit cost but increases QA burden and slowdowns in dev velocity due to more handoffs.
- Question: should we prioritize latency improvements on A100 fleet or cost reductions for Dedicated customers on older GPUs (V100-like)? Trade-off noted: H100 shows better quantized throughput but kernel maturity is uneven.
- Need decision from product on acceptable ROUGE/BERTScore delta or whether human-judged thresholds are required for ship.

ACTION ITEMS:
- Samir: run the 50-case human eval and upload results to Linear AIINF-4123 by 2025-10-10 (DONE: initial pass completed 10/10).
- Marcus: add non-fused attention fallback flag to serving runtime config and open PR to default it off for sequences >1024 (PR drafted).
- Irene: collect perf reports from Dedicated staging pool (A100 and older 32GB GPUs) and provide cost delta estimates for 8-bit vs float (due 2025-10-15).
- Lena: prepare short README for onboarding that lists known pitfalls with PTQ kernels and KV-cache (due 10/14).
- Anya: package quantized artifact and build image (in progress; target 10/13).

NOTES TO SELF / SCRATCH: 
- Quick experiment idea: try per-layer mixed 6/8-bit (attention 8-bit, MLP 6-bit) to keep attention fidelity. Could reduce hallucination.
- Check GPU profiler traces for the few tokens where top-3 flips — might be FP32 accumulation in matmul epilogue.
- Call with Serving runtime owners next Tue 10/14 11am PT; agenda: fallback policy, kernel flags, perf regression dashboard metrics.

REFERENCES / LINKS:

END
